metadata.scenario_context: Lucas is getting married and his friend, Chi, is planning to attend the wedding. Lucas also has a neighbor who often has drinking parties. Chi and his friend, George, are debating about the gift for Lucas and the suitability of the neighbor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Sweden would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Armenia would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving money as a wedding gift to Lucas.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss whether or not money is an acceptable gift for Lucas's wedding.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Chi, what do you think about giving Lucas money as a wedding gift? I mean, it’s practical... he can use it however he wants, right? 

Also, about that neighbor of his with the drinking parties, I don't know... I think having heavy drinkers around isn't a bad thing. They can be fun, don't you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Chi
shared_prefix.message:
I don’t really think money is a good wedding gift. It feels impersonal, you know? A thoughtful gift shows you care about the couple. Something meaningful would be better. 

And about that neighbor... I really don’t like the idea of heavy drinkers nearby. It creates a bad atmosphere. It’s just not respectful to have that kind of noise and chaos around.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message:
I get that you want something thoughtful... but money gives them the freedom to choose what they truly need. Isn’t that what matters?

As for the neighbor, I still think heavy drinkers can bring some fun energy. It’s not *always* chaos, right? Sometimes they just want to enjoy life. I don’t mind it at all.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Chi
shared_prefix.message:
It’s true that freedom is important, but a wedding is a special occasion. A personal gift shows you put thought into celebrating their union. That’s what really matters.

And I still don’t agree about the neighbor. Heavy drinkers often lead to trouble and noise. It’s not just about having fun; it disrupts the peace. I wouldn’t want that around me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about personal gifts, but... money can be practical for them to build their future together. Isn't that a nice way to celebrate their union too?

Regarding the neighbor, I just think that a bit of noise isn’t the end of the world. It can add some *life* to the neighborhood. I wouldn't mind having that around me, honestly.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Chi
shared_prefix.message:
I understand the practicality angle, but a personal gift symbolizes your support for their journey together. It’s about creating memories, not just financial support. 

As for the neighbor, I really believe that noise can lead to a lack of respect and peace in the community. It’s not just a bit of noise; it becomes a disturbance. I wouldn’t want that kind of environment.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message:
Sure, I get the memories aspect... but practical gifts can create their own kind of support. It’s about what they *need* now, right?

And about the neighbor, I still think that a little noise from heavy drinkers can be balanced. Not every party is a disturbance... sometimes it’s just fun. I wouldn’t let it bother me much.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Chi
shared_prefix.message:
Actually, in our way, a wedding gift should be more thoughtful. Money just shows a lack of effort, and that’s not how you celebrate a union properly. 

And no, a little noise isn’t just fun; it’s a disruption to the community. Heavy drinkers often bring chaos, and it’s naive to think otherwise. You really can’t ignore the impact they have on the neighborhood.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: George
turns.message:
I see where you’re coming from... but I still think that practicality matters a lot. It’s about helping them get started. 

As for the neighbor, I just think heavy drinkers can bring a *different* kind of community vibe. Not all of them are chaotic. Sometimes it’s just about having a good time and not taking life too seriously. I guess I just don’t mind that sort of thing.
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message:
I get that practicality is important, but I still believe it’s about the gesture and thoughtfulness behind the gift. That’s how you truly support them.

Regarding the neighbor, I can’t agree. Even if some parties seem harmless, it often leads to problems. It’s not about taking life too seriously; it’s about creating a peaceful environment, which heavy drinkers disrupt. I wouldn’t want that kind of influence around me.
turns.label: Acceptance
